instructions: Wrap the 1 lb flank steak in plastic wrap and put it in the freezer for 30 minutes. Firm steak is much easier to slice thinly.

While it firms up, rinse the 1 1/2 cups jasmine rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes, then take it off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, grate the 3 garlic cloves and 1 tsp of the ginger into a bowl. Add 1/2 cup hot water, the 6 tbsp soy sauce, 3 tbsp brown sugar, 1 1/2 tbsp cornstarch, 1/4 tsp black pepper and 2 tbsp sesame oil. Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Cut the 1 lb broccoli into bite sized florets. You should have about 6 cups.
Take the steak out of the freezer and slice it as thinly as you can against the grain, then cut the slices into bite sized strips. Sprinkle the 1/4 tsp salt over them.
Toast the 2 tsp sesame seeds in a large dry skillet over medium for about 2 minutes, shaking the pan, until they're golden. Transfer them into a small bowl.

Add 1 tbsp of the oil to the same skillet over medium. Add the broccoli and toss it for 1 minute, then add 2 tbsp water and set the lid on loosely. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, tossing a couple of times, until it's bright green and tender but still has some bite. Transfer it onto a plate.

Turn the heat to high and add 1 tbsp of the oil. Lay half the beef in a single layer and leave it for about 1 1/2 minutes, until the underside is browned. Flip the pieces and cook the other side for 1 minute. Move them to a plate.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil and cook the rest of the beef the same way.

Put all the beef back in the pan. Stir the sauce again and pour it in. Turn the heat to medium low and let it simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick and coats the beef.
Add the broccoli and toss until it's coated and hot. If the sauce is very thick, stir in a tablespoon or two of water.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve over the rice with the toasted sesame seeds on top.
method_notes: Both versions sear thinly sliced steak on high heat, cook the broccoli separately until crisp tender, and bring them together in a soy sauce thickened with cornstarch, served over rice. Natasha's Kitchen freezes flank steak briefly for easier slicing, makes a sweet sauce of soy, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic and ginger, and simmers the beef in it for a few minutes. Once Upon a Chef marinates flat iron steak in soy and Shaoxing wine, steams the broccoli with a splash of water, and uses oyster sauce and chicken broth in a lighter sauce cooked for under a minute. This one follows Natasha's Kitchen, with the beef seared in two batches and the broccoli steamed briefly in the pan.
